cohort: The study included 7,288 cases of preterm and full-term deliveries from two urban hospitals in a typical river valley-type city between January 2018 and December 2019.
finding: Maternal exposure to PM2.5, PM10, NO2, and CO was associated with an increased risk of preterm birth in mid-pregnancy (T2) and late pregnancy (T3), while SO2 exposure was linked to increased risk in mid-pregnancy (T2).
